# RAIBITSERVER

RAIBITSERVER is a container-first PaaS + DBaaS for clubs, schools, and small teams.
Production public site: https://raibit.kr/
Production console: https://console.raibit.kr/
Repository: https://github.com/jsk1004ha/RaibitServer

- Central handbook: docs/handbook/README.md

## Architecture

- apps/dashboard: Next.js dashboard
- apps/api: NestJS control-plane API
- apps/cli: API client CLI
- packages/core: deterministic TypeScript product and desired-state logic
- services/builder: Go build worker
- services/orchestrator: Go Kubernetes reconciler
- services/provisioner: Go managed-resource reconciler
- services/log-ingester and services/metrics-ingester: runtime telemetry ingestion
- infra: Helm, Kubernetes and Terraform

The API stores desired state. Long-running build, registry, Kubernetes, and provider work belongs to Go workers.

## Hard invariants

- Tenant workloads resolve to container images and Kubernetes desired state.
- A user Dockerfile takes precedence over framework detection.
- Production source checkout currently accepts exact https://github.com/owner/repo URLs; private repositories require a verified GitHub App installation.
- Prebuilt images must use an immutable registry/repository@sha256:<digest> reference. ZIP, GitLab, and Bitbucket are not current live-ingestion paths; local source is development-only.
- Only a preview deployment carrying a GitHub pull-request number has an isolated preview identity. Do not treat a manual preview without a PR number as isolated from production.
- Generated tenant routes use flat single-label hostnames under the configured base domain.
- Managed databases, caches, storage, vectors, and queues are catalog resources, not arbitrary compose containers.
- Tenant workloads are namespace-isolated and may not use privileged, root, hostPath, host networking, host PID/IPC, added capabilities, or service-account token automount.
- Secrets use encrypted values or provider-owned Secret references and must never appear in Git, prompts, logs, or API output.
- AI may recommend order but may not override deterministic security findings, RBAC, quota, scan, signature, or admission policy.
- Local verification must not require production credentials.

## Tenant application contract

- Bind the service to 0.0.0.0 on the configured port; core default is 8080.
- Run as non-root and support a read-only root filesystem; use /tmp only for temporary files.
- Prefer fast liveness and readiness endpoints for post-deploy HTTP checks. They are not currently wired as automatic tenant Kubernetes probes.
- Handle SIGTERM and stop gracefully.
- Store persistent data in an attached managed resource, not the container filesystem.
- Read configuration from environment variables.
- Never commit a real .env file.
- Use DATABASE_URL for an attached PostgreSQL resource when available.
- Treat migrations as an explicit, idempotent application or job responsibility.

## Safe deployment loop

1. Authenticate without printing tokens.
2. Query actual organization, project, service, and resource IDs.
3. Verify the remote branch and full expected commit SHA.
4. Create one deployment request.
5. Poll the returned deployment ID to READY, BUILD_FAILED, FAILED, or CANCELLED.
6. Match deployment commit SHA and image digest to the intended release.
7. Treat READY as a rollout state, then separately verify public HTTP, any app health endpoints, core behavior, and browser console.
8. For DB apps, perform a unique write/read and verify persistence after redeploy.
9. Verify runtime log ingestion.
10. Report evidence and remaining risks; do not infer missing values.

A 202 response means queued, not deployed. Do not update deployment status directly; status writers are trusted system actors.

## Destructive and production actions

Project, service, resource, database-data deletion, rollback, production Helm changes, secret rotation, and security-policy changes require explicit user scope and exact target verification. Do not bypass a 409 or fail-closed check.

## Platform verification

Use the repository package manager pinned in package.json.

pnpm test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
pnpm prisma:validate
pnpm prisma:generate
node scripts/check-structure.js
node src/cli.js validate examples/project.json
node src/cli.js manifest examples/project.json
node src/cli.js compose examples/docker-compose.yml
pnpm e2e:dry

When Go is available, run go test ./... and go build ./... in each changed services/* module.

## Completion evidence

Report changed files, exact source commit, CI result, deployment ID, deployment status, image digest, public URL, HTTP result, DB evidence when applicable, Pod readiness/restarts, runtime-log evidence, tests run, and remaining risks. Redact all credentials and connection strings.
